volume: 第二卷腐流部 Volume 2: Decaying Currents Department

stories.text: 一教官辭朝見象，低徊留之不忍去。人問其故，答曰：「我想祭丁的豬羊，有這般肥大便好。」
stories.translation: A teacher-official bidding farewell to the imperial court saw an elephant, and with lingering reluctance, he could not bear to leave. Someone asked him the reason, and he replied, "If my pigs and sheep for sacrificing on Ding days were this fat and large, it would be good."

stories.text: 歲貢選教職，初上任，其妻進衙，不覺放聲大哭。夫驚問之，妻曰：「我巴得你到今日，只道出了學門，誰知反進了學門。」
stories.translation: A teacher-official selected through the annual tribute system, upon first assuming office, had his wife enter the yamen (government office), and she could not help but burst into loud weeping. Her husband was startled and asked her, to which the wife replied, "I have longed for you to reach this day, thinking that we would finally be out of the school gate; who knew instead we are back into the school gate."

stories.text: 祭丁過，兩廣文爭一豬大臟，各執其臟之一頭。一廣文稍強，盡掣得其臟，爭者止兩手擼得臟中油一捧而已。因曰：「予雖不得大葬（臟），君無尤（油）焉。」
stories.translation: After the Ding sacrifice, two scholars from Guangdong and Guangxi quarreled over a large pig's offal, each holding one end of it. One scholar was slightly stronger and managed to pull the entire offal away, while the other, who had lost the struggle, only managed to rub his hands together and got a handful of grease from it. He then said, "Although I did not get the large offal (zang), you have no grease (you) to blame me for."

stories.text: 教官子與縣丞子廝打，教官子屢負，歸而哭訴其母。母曰：「彼家終日吃肉，故恁般強健會打。你家終日吃腐，力氣衰微，如何敵得他過？」教官曰：「這般我兒不要忙，等祭過了丁，再與他報復便了。」
stories.translation: The son of a teacher-official and the son of the county assistant official fought, with the son of the teacher-official losing repeatedly. He returned home and wept to his mother, complaining about it. The mother said, "Their family eats meat all day long; that is why they are so strong and good at fighting." "Your family eats tofu all day, your strength is weak, how can you possibly beat them?" The teacher-official said, "Do not worry, my son. Wait until after the Ding sacrifice is over, and then I will take revenge for you."

stories.text: 鼠與黃蜂拜為兄弟，邀一秀才做盟證，秀才不得已往，列為第三人。一友問曰：「兄何居乎鼠輩之下？」答曰：「他兩個一會鑽，一會刺，我只得讓他罷了。」
stories.translation: A rat and a yellow wasp became sworn brothers, inviting a xiucai to be their witness. Having no alternative, the xiucai went, becoming the third person in attendance. A friend asked, "Brother, why do you take a position beneath such a rat?" He replied, "The two of them are one who drills and one who stings; I have no choice but to let them go ahead."

stories.text: 兩道學先生議論不合，各自詫真道學而互詆為假，久之不決。乃請正于孔子，孔子下階，鞠躬致敬而言曰：「吾道甚大，何必相同。二位老先生皆真正道學，丘素所欽仰，豈有偽哉。」兩人各大喜而退。弟子曰：「夫子何諛之甚也！」孔子曰：「此輩人哄得他動身就夠了，惹他怎麼？」
stories.translation: Two Neo-Confucian scholars had a disagreement in their discussion, each claiming to be the true adherent of Daoxue while accusing the other of being false. After a long time, they could not reach a decision. They then invited Confucius to adjudicate the matter. Confucius descended from his seat, bowed respectfully, and said, "My Way is vast; why must we be identical?" "The two elder scholars are both truly adherents of Daoxue, whom I have long admired; how could there be any pretense?" The two men were greatly pleased and departed. A disciple said, "Master, why did you flatter them so much!" Confucius replied, "It is enough to have convinced these people to move; how can I provoke them further?"

stories.text: 道學先生嫁女出門，至半夜，尚在廳前徘徊踱索。僕云：「相公，夜深請睡罷。」先生頓足怒云：「你不曉得，小畜生此時正在那裏放肆了！」
stories.translation: A Neo-Confucian scholar sent his daughter off in marriage, and until midnight, he still lingered and paced back and forth before the hall. The servant said, "Master, it is late; please go to sleep." The scholar stamped his foot in anger and said, "Don't you know? That little brat is being outrageous there right now!"

stories.text: 廣文到任，門人以錢五十為贄者，題刺曰：「謹具贄儀五十文，門人某百頓首拜。」師書其帖而返之，曰：「減去五十拜，補足一百文何如？」門人答曰：「情願一百五十拜，免了這五十文又何如？」
stories.translation: When a scholar-official from Guangwen arrived at his post, one of his disciples presented fifty coins as a gift, writing on the visiting card: "With respectful submission of this presentation gift of fifty cash, disciple bows in deep reverence." The teacher wrote on the note and returned it, saying, "Reduce fifty bows to one hundred cash; how about that?" The disciple replied, "I would rather bow 150 times and do away with the fifty cash; how about that?"

stories.text: 一士夫子孫繁衍，而同儕有無子者，乃驕語之曰：「爾沒力量，兒子也養不出一個。像我這等子孫多，何等熱鬧。」同儕答曰：「其子爾力也，其孫非爾力也。」
stories.translation: A scholar's descendants were numerous, and when he saw a peer who had no children, he boasted, "You have no strength; you can't even raise one son." "Like me with so many descendants, how lively and bustling it is!" The peer replied, "Those sons are your effort; but the grandchildren are not your effort."

stories.text: 孔子在陳絕糧，命顏子往回回國借之，以其名與國號相同，冀有情熟。比往通訖，大怒曰：「汝孔子要攘夷狄，怪俺回回，平日又罵俺回之為人也擇（賊）乎！」糧斷不與。顏子怏怏而歸。子貢請往，自稱平昔極奉承，常曰：「賜也何敢望回回。」群回大喜，以白糧一擔，先令攜去，許以陸續運付。子貢歸，述之夫子，孔子攢眉曰：「糧便騙了一擔，只是文理不通。」
stories.translation: Confucius was in Chen and ran out of food, so he ordered Yanzi to go to the state of Huo to borrow some. He did this because Yanzi's name coincided with the state's title, hoping for a favorable reception due to their similarity. After Yanzi arrived and explained the situation, they became very angry and said, "You Confucius want to expel the Yi and Di peoples, you blame us Huizi (Hui people), yet in daily life, do you also call us thieves?" They refused to give any grain. Yanzi returned in a sullen and dejected mood. Zigong volunteered to go, claiming that he had always been very respectful in the past and often said, "How dare I, Zi, compare myself to the Hui people?" The group of Hui people were very pleased and gave him one dan (about 100 catties) of white grain to take away first, promising to send more in installments. Zigong returned and reported this to Confucius, who frowned and said, "Although we were tricked into getting one dan of grain, the reasoning just doesn't make sense."

stories.text: 糧長收糧在倉廩內，耗鼠甚多，潛伺之，見黃鼠群食其中。開倉掩捕，黃鼠有護身屁，連放數個。糧長大怒曰：「這樣放屁畜生，也被他吃了糧去。」
stories.translation: The head in charge of collecting grain found that there was significant loss from the granaries and secretly watched, discovering a large number of yellow rats feasting on the grain inside. When he opened the granary to capture them, the yellow rats had protective flatulence and released several in succession. The grain officer became very angry and said, "Such a farting beast has also eaten the grain."

stories.text: 其年鄉試，一縣脫科。諸生請堪輿來看風水，以泥塑聖像卵小，不相稱故耳。遂喚妝佛匠改造。聖人大喝曰：「這班不通文理的畜生，你們自不讀書，干我卵甚事！」
stories.translation: In that year's provincial examination, one county failed to produce any successful candidates. The students invited a geomancer to examine the feng shui, because the clay statue of Confucius had an undersized head, which was considered inappropriate. They then summoned a Buddhist image craftsman to modify it. The sage shouted angrily, "You bunch of illiterate brutes! You yourselves don't study; what business is it of my head?"

stories.text: 三秀才往妓家設東敘飲，內一秀才曰：「兄治何經？」曰：「通《詩經》。」復問其次，曰：「通《書經》。」因戲問妓曰：「汝通何經？」曰：「妾通月經。」眾皆大笑。妓曰：「列位相公休笑我，你們做秀才，都從這紅門中出來的。」
stories.translation: Three xiucai scholars went to a courtesan's home for a banquet, and one of them asked, "Brother, which classic are you studying?" The other replied, "I have mastered the Classic of Poetry." They asked again about the second one, and he said, "I have mastered the Book of Documents." Then they jokingly asked the courtesan, "Which classic are you familiar with?" She replied, "I am familiar with my menstrual cycle." Everyone laughed heartily. The courtesan said, "Gentlemen, don't laugh at me; you all became xiucai by passing through this red gate."

stories.text: 甲乙二士應試，甲曰：「我夢一木沖天，何如？」乙曰：「一木沖天，乃『未』字也，恐非佳兆。」因言己「夢一雉貼天而飛，此必文門之象，穩中無疑矣。」甲搖首曰：「咦，野（也）味（未）。」
stories.translation: Two scholars, Jia and Yi, were about to take an examination. Jia said, "I had a dream in which a tree pierced the sky; what do you think?" Yi replied, "One tree piercing the sky is the character 'Wei,' which probably isn't a good omen." Yi then said that he had dreamed of "a pheasant flying close to the sky," which must be an omen for success in the literary examination, and there was no doubt about it. Jia shook his head and said, "Ah, wild (ye) flavor (wei)."

stories.text: 秀才詰問和尚曰：「你們經典內『南無』二字，只應念本音，為何念作那摩？」僧亦回問云：「相公，《四書》上『於戲』二字，為何亦讀作嗚呼？如今相公若讀於戲，小僧就念南無。相公若是嗚呼，小僧自然要那摩。」
stories.translation: A xiucai scholar questioned a monk, saying, "In your scriptures, the two characters 'Nan Wu' should be pronounced according to their original sounds; why do you pronounce them as 'Na Mo'?" The monk also asked in return, "Master, why is the phrase 'Yu Xi' in the Four Books also read as 'Wu Hu'?" "Now if Master reads 'Yu Xi,' I will chant 'Nan Wu.'" "If Master says 'Wu Hu,' naturally, I shall chant 'Na Mo.'"

stories.text: 一人問曰：「相公尊姓？」曰：「姓楊。」其人曰：「既是羊，為甚無角？」士怒曰：「呆狗入出的！」那人錯會其意，曰：「嗄！」
stories.translation: A person asked, "What is your esteemed surname, Master?" He replied, "Yang." The person said, "If you are a sheep, why do you have no horns?" The scholar angrily said, "You foolish dog!" Hearing this, the man misunderstood and exclaimed, "Ah!"

stories.text: 玉帝生日，群仙畢賀。東方朔後至，見壽星傍惶門外，問之，曰：「有告示貼出，不放我進。」又問：「何故貼出？」答曰：「怪我頭長（場）。」
stories.translation: On the birthday of the Jade Emperor, all the immortals gathered to offer their congratulations. Dongfang Shuo arrived late and saw the Star of Longevity anxiously waiting outside the gate. He asked why, and was told, "There is a notice posted; they will not let me in." Dongfang Shuo then asked, "Why did they post it?" The reply was, "Because of my long head (exam hall)."

stories.text: 賓主二人同睡，客索夜壺。主人說：「在床下，未曾倒得。」只好棚過頭一場，後場斷斷再來不得了。
stories.translation: A guest and his host were sleeping together, when the guest asked for a chamber pot at night. The host said, "It is under the bed; I haven't emptied it yet." The guest had no choice but to cross over to the first hall (exam room), and certainly could not come back for the later examination halls.

stories.text: 一瞎子雙目不明，善能聞香識氣。有秀才拿一《西廂》本與他聞，曰：「《西廂記》。」問：「何以知之？」答曰：「有些脂粉氣。」又拿《三國志》與他聞，曰：「《三國志》。」又問：「何以知之。」答曰：「有些刀兵氣。」秀才以為奇異，卻將自做的文字與他聞，瞎子曰：「此是你的佳作。」問：「你怎知？」答曰：「有些屁氣。」
stories.translation: A blind man, though unable to see with his eyes, was skilled at identifying things by their scent and qi. A xiucai presented a copy of "The Western Chamber" to him, and the blind man said, "It is 'The Western Chamber.'" He was asked, "How do you know that?" The blind man replied, "It has a scent of powder and rouge." He was then given a copy of Records of the Three Kingdoms to smell, and he said, "It is the Records of the Three Kingdoms." Again they asked, "How do you know this?" He replied, "It has the smell of swords and warfare." The xiucai thought it remarkable, so he presented his own writings for the blind man to smell. The blind man said, "This is your excellent work." He was asked, "How do you know?" The blind man replied, "It has a smell of flatulence."

stories.text: 有盛大、盛二者，所戴氈帽，合放一處。一被蟲蛀，兄弟二人互相推競，各認其不蛀者奪之。適一士經過，以其讀書人明理，請彼決之。士執蛀帽反覆細看，乃睨盛大曰：「此汝帽也！」問：「何以見得？」士曰：「豈不聞《大學》注解云：『宣（先）著（蛀），盛大之貌（帽）』。」
stories.translation: There were two men named Sheng Da and Sheng Er, whose felt hats had been placed together in one location. One of the hats was eaten by moths, and the two brothers argued with each other, each claiming that the undamaged hat should be taken from the other. Just then a scholar passed by, and since he was considered to be an educated man who understood reason, they asked him to decide the matter. The scholar took the moth-eaten hat and examined it carefully back and forth, then glanced at Sheng Da and said, "This is your hat!" He was asked, "On what basis do you say that?" The scholar said, "Have you not heard the commentary on The Great Learning say: 'Xuan (first) Zhu (moth-eaten), is the appearance of Sheng Da's hat'?"

stories.text: 窮人往各寺院，竊取神物靈心，止有土地廟未取。及去挖開，見空空如也。乃駭嘆曰：「看他巾便帶了一頂，原來腹中毫無一物！」
stories.translation: A poor man went to various temples and stole sacred objects, but had not yet taken anything from the Earth God Temple. When he finally went there and dug it up, he found it completely empty. He was startled and exclaimed, "Looking at his headscarf, he already wore a hat on it; originally there was absolutely nothing inside his belly!"

stories.text: 一和尚撒尿，玩弄自己陽物。偶有帶巾人走來，戲曰：「你師徒兩個，在此講甚麼？」和尚曰：「看他頭有幾多大，要折頂方巾與他帶帶。」
stories.translation: A monk urinated, playing with his own penis. By chance a man wearing a headscarf passed by and teased, saying, "You two master and disciple, what are you talking about here?" The monk said, "Look at how big his head is; I need to fold a square headscarf for him to wear."

stories.text: 有初死見冥王者，王謂其生前受用太過，判來生去做一秀才，與以五子。鬼吏稟曰：「此人罪重，不應如此善遣。」王笑曰：「正惟罪重，我要處他一個窮秀才，把他許多兒子，活活累殺他罷了。」
stories.translation: There was a recently deceased person who appeared before the King of Hell, and the king said that since he had enjoyed too much in life, he would be reborn as a xiucai for his next life. He was given five sons. A ghost official reported, "This man committed grave sins and should not be sent so kindly." The king laughed and said, "Precisely because his sins are so great, I want to make him a poor xiucai; by giving him many sons, they will exhaust and kill him alive."

stories.text: 一士死見冥王，自稱飽學，博古通今。王偶撒一屁，士即進詞云：「伏惟大王高聳金臀，洪宣寶屁，依稀乎絲竹之聲，仿佛乎麝蘭之氣。臣立下風，不勝馨香之味。」王喜，命賜宴，准與陽壽一紀，至期自來報到，不消鬼卒勾引。士過十二年，復詣陰司，謂門上曰：「煩到大王處通稟，說十年前做放屁文章的秀才又來了。」
stories.translation: A scholar died and appeared before the King of Hell; he claimed to be well-versed, knowledgeable in both ancient and modern times. The king happened to pass gas, and the scholar immediately presented a verse saying, "Your Majesty's lofty golden buttocks emit a precious fart; it faintly resembles the sound of zithers and flutes, and vaguely carries the fragrance of musk and orchid. Standing downwind, I cannot help but savor its fragrant aroma." The king was pleased and ordered a banquet, granting him twelve more years of life. When the time came, he would return on his own without needing to be summoned by ghost soldiers. After twelve years, the scholar returned to the Underworld and said to a gatekeeper, "Please go inform the great king that the xiucai who once wrote an ode to farting has come back after ten years."

stories.text: 儒學碑亭新完，一士攜妓往視，見碑下負重，戲謂妓曰：「汝父在此，為何不拜？」妓即下拜云：「我你爺，看你這等蹭蹬，何時得出學門！」
stories.translation: A new stele pavilion for Confucian learning had just been completed. A scholar brought a courtesan to see it, and seeing someone carrying heavy loads beneath the stele, he teased the courtesan by saying, "Your father is here; why don't you pay your respects?" The courtesan immediately knelt and said, "I am your father. Looking at how you are so down on your luck, when will you ever leave the school gate!"

stories.text: 東家喪妻母，往祭，托館師撰文。乃按古本誤抄祭妻父者與之，為識者看出，主人怪而責之。館師曰：「此文是古本刊定的，如何得錯？只怕倒是他家錯死了人，這便不關我事。」
stories.translation: The neighbor lost his mother-in-law and went to pay respects, entrusting the schoolteacher with writing an elegy for her. However, he mistakenly copied a eulogy meant for mourning one's wife's father from an old manuscript and gave it to the neighbor. Someone who recognized this pointed it out, and the host scolded him angrily. The schoolteacher said, "This text was published in an ancient edition; how could there be a mistake?" "I only fear that perhaps they mistakenly mourned the wrong person. If so, it is not my fault."

stories.text: 一秀士新娶，夜分就寢，問于新婦曰：「吾欲雲雨，不知娘子尊意允否？」新人曰：「官人從心所欲。」士曰：「既蒙俯允，請娘子展股開肱，學生無禮又無禮矣。」及舉事，新婦曰：「痛哉，痛哉！」秀才曰：「徐徐而進之，渾身通泰矣。」
stories.translation: A young scholar had just married, and at night he went to bed. He asked his new bride, "I wish to have intimacy; I wonder if you would be willing, my dear?" The newlywed replied, "Husband, do as your heart desires." The scholar said, "Since you have kindly agreed, please open your legs and arms for me. I shall be impolite once again." When the act began, the new bride cried out in pain, "It hurts! It hurts!" The xiucai said, "Go slowly and gently; soon your whole body will feel relaxed and comfortable."

stories.text: 租戶連年欠租，每推田瘦做不出米來。士怒曰：「明年待我自種，看是如何？」租戶曰：「憑相公拚著命去種，到底是做不出的。」
stories.translation: The tenant had been in arrears on rent for several years, always claiming that the land was barren and could not yield rice. The scholar became angry and said, "Next year I will plant it myself; let's see what happens!" The tenant replied, "Even if you, Sir, risk your life to cultivate it, in the end, it still cannot produce anything."

stories.text: 一士子赴試，艱于構思。諸生隨牌俱出。接考者候久，甲僕問乙僕曰：「不知作文一篇，約有多少字？」乙曰：「想來不過五六百。」甲曰：「五六百字，難道胸中便沒有了，此時還不出來？」乙曰：「五六百字雖有在肚裡，只是一時湊不起來耳。」
stories.translation: A scholar went for an examination but had difficulty in composing his answers. All the students followed and left together. The examiner had been waiting for a long time, so one servant asked another, "I wonder how many characters are in an essay?" The second servant replied, "It must be no more than five or six hundred." The first servant said, "Five or six hundred characters—could there really be nothing in his mind? Why hasn't he come out by now?" The second servant replied, "Although there may be five or six hundred characters in his belly, it's just that he can't put them together at the moment."

stories.text: 兩秀才同時四等，於受責時曾識一面。後聯姻，會親日相見。男親家曰：「尊容曾在何處會過來？」女親家曰：「便是有些面善，一時想不起。」各沉吟間，忽然同悟，男親家點頭曰：「嗄。」女親家亦點頭曰：「嗄。」
stories.translation: Two xiucai were both of the fourth degree, and they had once met briefly when receiving punishment. Later, their families became in-laws, and on the day of a family gathering, they met again. The groom's relative said, "Your face seems familiar; where have we met before?" The bride's relative replied, "It does seem somewhat familiar, but I can't recall at the moment." While both were pondering in silence, they suddenly realized together. The groom's relative nodded and said, "Ah!" The bride's relative also nodded and said, "Ah!"

stories.text: 一士考末等，自覺慚愧，且慮其妻之姍己也。乃架一說誑妻曰：「從前宗師止于六等，今番遇著這個瘟官，好不利害，又增出一等，你道可惡不可惡？」妻曰：「七等如何？」對曰：「六等不過去前程，考七等者，竟要閹割。」妻大驚曰：「這等，你考在何處？」夫曰：「還虧我爭氣，考在六等，幸而免割。」
stories.translation: A scholar ranked last in the examination, felt ashamed, and also feared that his wife would look down on him. So he lied to his wife, saying, "In the past, the examiner only ranked up to sixth place. This time we encountered this wretched official; it was very unfair of him to add another rank. Don't you think it's outrageous?" His wife asked, "What is seventh rank like?" He replied, "Those ranked sixth are merely denied future prospects. But those ranked seventh must actually be castrated." His wife was greatly shocked and asked, "If that is the case, where did you rank?" The husband said, "Thankfully I was enterprising enough to rank sixth; fortunately, I escaped castration."

stories.text: 一秀才將試，日夜懮鬱不已。妻乃慰之曰：「看你作文，如此之難，好似奴生產一般。」夫曰：「還是你每生子容易。」妻曰：「怎見得？」夫曰：「你是有在肚裏的，我是沒在肚裡的。」
stories.translation: A xiucai was about to take an examination and had been worrying day and night without ceasing. His wife comforted him, saying, "Looking at how difficult it is for you to write an essay, it seems just like the pain of me giving birth." The husband said, "Still, your childbirth must be easier." His wife asked, "How do you know that?" The husband replied, "Because your child is actually in your belly, but mine isn't even there."

stories.text: 一生不完卷，考置四等，受撲。對友曰：「我只缺得半篇。」友云：「還好。若做完，看了定要打殺。」
stories.translation: A student who did not complete his exam paper was ranked fourth and received a beating. He said to his friend, "I only missed half of the essay." The friend replied, "That's still good. If you had finished it, they would have surely beaten you to death upon reading it."

stories.text: 一士歲考求簽，通陳曰：「考在六等求上上，四等下下。」廟祝曰：「相公差矣，四等止杖責，如何反是下下？」士曰：「非汝所知。六等黜退，極是乾淨。若是四等，看了我的文字，決被打殺。」
stories.translation: A scholar sought an oracle before the annual examination, and it was said: "If you rank sixth, seek the highest; if fourth, the lowest." The temple official said, "Sir is mistaken. Ranking fourth only results in a beating with a stick; how can it be considered the worst?" The scholar replied, "That is not something you understand." Ranking sixth means being dismissed completely and cleanly. But if I rank fourth, they will read my essays and definitely beat me to death."

stories.text: 府取童生，祈夢：「道考可望入泮否？」神問曰：「汝祖父是科下否？」曰：「不是。」又問：「家中富饒否？」曰：「無得。」神笑曰：「既是這等，你做甚麼夢！」
stories.translation: A county official selected child students and prayed in a dream, "Is there any hope that I can enter the school?" The deity asked, "Did your grandfather ever pass an examination?" He replied, "No." The deity then asked, "Is your family wealthy?" He replied, "No." The deity laughed and said, "If it is like this, then why are you having such a dream!"

stories.text: 有以銀錢夤緣入泮者，拜謁孔廟，孔子下席答之。士曰：「今日是夫子弟子禮，應坐受。」孔子曰：「豈敢。你是我孔方兄的弟子，斷不受拜。」
stories.translation: There was someone who had bribed his way into the school and, upon visiting the Confucius Temple, paid homage. Confucius himself descended from the dais to receive him. A scholar said, "Today is a ceremony for the disciples of Master Kong; you should sit and accept it." Confucius said, "How could I dare to?" "You are a disciple of Kong Fangxiong, and certainly should not receive my bow."

stories.text: 館師歲暮買舟回家，舟子問曰：「相公貴庚？」答曰：「屬狗的，開年已是五十歲了。」舟人曰：「我也屬狗，為何貴賤不等？」又問：「那一月生的？」答曰：「正月。」舟子大悟曰：「是了，是了，怪不得！我十二月生，是個狗尾，所以搖了這一世。相公正月生，是個狗頭，所以教（叫）了這一世。」
stories.translation: At the end of the year, a tutor bought a boat to return home. The boatman asked, "Master, how old are you?" He replied, "I was born in the Year of the Dog; next year I will already be fifty years old." The boatman said, "I am also a dog zodiac sign. Why is there such an inequality between us?" He then asked, "Which month were you born in?" He replied, "The first lunar month." The boatman suddenly realized and said, "Ah! I see now, no wonder!" "I was born in the twelfth lunar month; I am a dog's tail. That is why I have wagged my tail all this life." "Master was born in the first lunar month, and is a dog's head. That is why you have barked all this life."

stories.title_en: A Dog Sitting as a Tutor.
stories.text: 一人慣會說謊，對親家云：「舍間有三寶：一牛每日能行千里，一雞每更止啼一聲，又一狗善能讀書。」親家駭云：「有此異事，來日必要登堂求看。」其人歸與妻述之：「一時說了謊，怎生回護？」妻曰：「不妨，我自有處。」次日，親家來訪，內云：「早上往北京去了。」問：「幾時回？」答曰：「七八日就來的。」又問：「為何能快？」曰：「騎了自家牛去。」問：「宅上還有報更雞？」適值亭中午雞啼，即指曰：「只此便是，不但夜裡報更，日間生客來也報的。」又問：「讀書狗請借一觀。」答曰：「不瞞親家說，只為家寒，出外坐館去了。」
stories.translation: A man was very good at lying. He told his in-laws, "In my home there are three treasures: a bull that can travel one thousand li every day; a chicken that only crows once per watch of the night; and also a dog who is excellent at reading books." His in-laws were astonished and said, "Such an extraordinary thing? Tomorrow I must visit your home to see them for myself." The man returned home and told his wife, "I have made a false claim. How can I cover it up?" His wife said, "Don't worry; I will take care of it." The next day, the in-laws came to visit. Inside, they were told, "He went to Beijing this morning." They asked, "When will he return?" The reply was, "He should be back in seven or eight days." They asked again, "Why can he return so quickly?" The reply was, "He rode our own bull there." They asked, "Is there also a rooster that crows to mark the watches of the night at your home?" Just then, a rooster crowed in the noon at the pavilion. They pointed to it and said, "This is exactly that one; not only does it announce the watches of the night, but it also crows when guests come during the day." They then asked, "Please let us see your dog who can read books." The reply was, "I will not hide this from my in-laws. Because our family is poor, he has gone out to work as a tutor."

stories.text: 一先生講書，至「康子饋藥」，徒問：「是煎藥是丸藥？」先生向主人誇獎曰：「非令郎美質不能問，非學生博學不能答。上節『鄉人儺」，儺的自然是丸藥。下節又是煎藥，不是用爐火，如何就『廄焚』起來！」
stories.translation: A teacher was lecturing on the classics, and when he reached the passage about "Kangzi offering medicine," a student asked, "Is it decocted medicine or pill medicine?" The teacher praised the host and said, "Only a son of such fine talent could ask this question, and only a student with broad learning could answer it." "In the previous section 'Xiangren Nuo,' naturally, 'Nuo' refers to pill medicine." "The next passage is again about decocted medicine. If it's not using a stove or fire, how could the 'stables burn down' so quickly!"

stories.text: 館師欲為固館計，每贊學生聰明。東家不信，命當面對課。師曰：「蟹。」學生對曰：「傘。」師贊之不已。東翁不解，師曰：「我有隱意，蟹乃橫行之物，令郎對『傘』，有獨立之意，豈不絕妙。」東翁又命對兩字課，師曰：「割稻。」學生對曰：「行房。」師又贊不已。東家大怒，師曰：「此對也有隱意，我出『割稻』者，乃積穀防飢。他對『行房』者，乃養兒待老。」
stories.translation: A tutor, wanting to ensure his position as a teacher, often praised the intelligence of his students. The host did not believe this and ordered an in-person examination for the student. The teacher said, "Crab." The student replied, "Umbrella." The teacher continued to praise him without ceasing. The host did not understand, so the teacher explained, "There is a hidden meaning here. A crab is a creature that moves sideways, but your son answered with 'umbrella,' which conveys an upright and independent spirit—how wonderful!" The host then ordered another two-character test. The teacher said, "Harvesting rice." The student replied, "Having a room to walk in." The teacher praised him again without ceasing. The host became very angry, but the teacher said, "This answer also has a hidden meaning. When I gave 'harvesting rice,' it meant storing grain to prevent famine." "His reply of 'having a room' means raising sons for old age support."

stories.text: 一師慣謀人館，被冥王訪知．著夜叉拿來。師躲在門內不出．鬼卒設計哄騙曰：「你快出來．有一好館請你。」師聞有館，即便趨出，被夜叉擒住。先生曰：「看你這鬼頭鬼腦，原不像個請先生的。」
stories.translation: A teacher who was accustomed to scheming for tutoring positions was discovered by the King of Hell, and Yecha demons were sent to bring him. The teacher hid inside the door and refused to come out, so the ghostly soldiers devised a plan to deceive him, saying, "Come out quickly! There is a good tutoring position waiting for you." Upon hearing there was a teaching position available, the teacher hurriedly came out and was immediately captured by the Yecha demons. The teacher said, "Looking at your ghostly appearance, you don't seem like someone who would invite a tutor."

stories.text: 一人見穩婆姿色美，欲誘之，乃假妝婦人將產，請來收生，穩婆摸著此物。大驚曰：「我收生多年矣，有頭先生者，名為順生；腳先生者，名為倒生；手先生者，名為橫生。這個雞巴先生，實是不曾見過。」
stories.translation: A man saw that a midwife was beautiful and wished to seduce her, so he pretended to be a woman about to give birth and invited her over. The midwife touched this object of his. She was greatly shocked and said, "I have been assisting in childbirth for many years. When the head comes first, it is called 'Shunsheng'; when the feet come first, it is called 'Daosheng'; and when the hands come first, it is known as 'Hengsheng.'" "But this 'jiba' coming first—I have never seen such a thing!"

stories.text: 夫妻夜臥，婦握夫陽具曰：「是人皆有表號，獨此物無一美稱，可贈他一號。」夫曰：「假者名為角先生，則真者當去一角字，竟呼為先生可也。」婦曰：「既是先生，有館在此，請他來坐。」雲雨既畢。次早，妻以雞子酒啖夫。夫笑曰：「我知你謝先生也，且問你先生何如？」妻曰：「先生盡好，只是嫌他略罷軟，沒坐性些。」
stories.translation: A husband and wife were lying in bed at night when the wife took her husband's penis in hand and said, "Everyone has a title or nickname, yet this thing alone lacks any beautiful name. We should give it one." The husband said, "If the fake ones are called 'Jiao Xiansheng,' then the real one should drop the word 'jiao' and simply be called 'Xiansheng.'" The wife said, "If it is a 'xiansheng,' there must be a teaching hall here. Let us invite him to sit." After they had finished their intimate act. The next morning, the wife gave her husband a drink of egg wine. The husband smiled and said, "I know you are thanking your 'xiansheng.' Let me ask you—how was he?" The wife replied, "The teacher was excellent overall, but I found him a bit too soft and lacking in staying power."

stories.text: 有兄弟兩人，共延一師，分班供給。每交班，必互嫌師瘦，怪供給之不豐。於是兄弟相約，師輪至日，即秤斤兩，以為交班肥瘦之驗。一日，弟將交師於兄，乃令師飽餐而去。既上秤，師偶撒一屁，乃咎之曰：「秤上買賣，豈可輕易撒出！說不得，原替我吃了下去。」
stories.translation: There were two brothers who jointly hired a teacher and divided the expenses for his support. Every time they took turns supporting the teacher, they would always complain about how thin he was and blame each other for not providing enough supplies. As a result, the brothers made an agreement that on the day their turn to support the teacher came around, they would weigh him in order to verify whether he had gained or lost weight during his stay. One day, when it was time for the younger brother to hand over the teacher to the older one, he made the teacher eat a full meal before leaving. When they put him on the scale, the teacher happened to pass gas, and the brothers scolded him, saying, "This is a business transaction based on weight—how could you casually let out a fart!" "You can't just say it's nothing; originally, I swallowed it for you."

stories.text: 庸師慣讀破句，又念白字。一日訓徒，教《大學序》，念云：「大學之，書古之，大學所以教人之。」主人知覺，怒而逐之。復被一蔭官延請入幕，官不識律令，每事詢之館師。一日，巡捕拿一盜鐘者至，官問：「何以治之？」師曰：「夫子之道（盜）忠（鐘），恕而已矣。」官遂釋放。又一日，獲一盜席者至，官又問，師曰：「朝聞道夕（席），死可矣。」官即將盜席者立斃杖下。適冥王私行，察訪得實，即命鬼判拿來，痛罵曰：「不通的畜生！你騙人館谷，誤人子弟，其罪不小，摘往輪回去變豬狗。」師再三哀告曰：「做豬狗固不敢辭，但豬要判生南方，狗乞做一母狗。」王問何故，答曰：「南方之（豬），強與北方之。」又問：「母狗為何？」答曰：「《曲禮》云：『臨財母苟（狗）得，臨難母苟免。』」
stories.translation: An unskilled teacher was accustomed to misreading sentences and also mispronouncing characters. One day, while teaching his students, he was instructing on the "Preface to the Great Learning" and read it as: "The Great Learning's book, ancient times' Great Learning, so the Great Learning teaches people." When the host became aware of this, he was furious and drove him away. Later, a government official who had obtained his position through favor invited the teacher to serve as an advisor. Since this official did not know legal statutes, he often consulted the tutor on matters of governance. One day, a patrol officer captured a thief who had stolen a bell and brought him before the official. The official asked, "How should we deal with this case?" The teacher said, "Confucius' way of dealing with loyalty (theft) and bells—mercy is all that is needed." The official then released the thief. Another day, an officer brought a thief who had stolen mats before the official. When asked again, the teacher said, "He who hears the Way in the morning may die (steal mats) at night." The official immediately had the mat thief beaten to death with a stick. At that moment, King Yama was making an incognito inspection and discovered the truth. He immediately ordered the ghostly judge to bring him in and scolded him fiercely, saying, "You ignorant beast!" "You deceived people into hiring you as a tutor, misleading their children. Your crime is great! Take him to the Wheel of Rebirth and make him be reborn as a pig or dog." The teacher pleaded repeatedly, saying, "I dare not refuse being reborn as a pig or a dog, but if I must be a pig, please assign me to be born in the south; and if I am to be a dog, I beg to be made a female dog." The King asked why, and the teacher replied, "Pigs in the south are stronger than those in the north." The King then asked, "Why a female dog?" He replied, "The Rites of Zhou states: 'When facing wealth, do not greedily (dog) obtain it; when facing danger, do not selfishly avoid it.'"

stories.text: 一師學淺，善讀別字。主人惡之，與師約，每讀一別字，除修一分。至歲終，退除將盡，止餘銀三分，封送之。師怒曰：「是何言興，是何言興（與）！」主人曰：「如今再扣二分，存銀一分矣。」東家母在傍曰：「一年辛若，半除也罷。」先生近前作謝曰：「夫人不言，言必有中。」主人曰：「恰好連這一分，乾淨拿進去。」
stories.translation: A teacher with shallow learning was good at misreading characters. The host disliked this and made an agreement with the teacher: for every character he misread, one coin of tuition would be deducted. By year's end, nearly all the tuition had been deducted, leaving only three coins in silver, which were then wrapped and sent to him. The teacher angrily said, "What kind of nonsense is this? What kind of nonsense!" The host replied, "Now I will deduct two more coins, and there will be just one coin left." The host's mother said from the side, "After a year of hard work, deducting half is enough." The teacher stepped forward and bowed in thanks, saying, "Madam did not speak lightly; when she speaks, her words are always to the point." The host said, "Well then, take this last coin and put it all in."

stories.text: 庸師慣讀別字。一夜，與徒講論前後《赤壁）兩賦，竟念「賦」字為「賊」字。適有偷兒潛伺窗外，師乃朗誦大言曰：「這前面《赤（作拆字）壁賊》呀。」賊大驚，因思前而既覺，不若往房後穿逾而入。時已夜深，師講完，往後房就寢。既上床，復與徒論及後面《赤壁賦》，亦如前讀。偷兒在外嘆息曰：「我前後行藏，悉被此人識破。人家請了這樣先生，看家狗都不消養得了！」
stories.translation: An unskilled teacher was accustomed to misreading characters. One night, while discussing the two "Odes to the Red Cliff" with his students, he mistakenly read the character for "fu" as "zei." At that moment, a thief was secretly watching from outside the window. The teacher then loudly recited, saying, "This 'Red Cliff Thief' in front." The thief was greatly startled and thought to himself: since the front had already been discovered, it would be better to go around to the back of the house and break in from there. It was now deep into the night; after finishing his lecture, the teacher went to the rear room to sleep. After getting into bed, he again discussed with his students the latter "Ode to the Red Cliff," reading it in the same mistaken way as before. The thief outside sighed and said, "This man has discovered both my front and back movements." "If a family hires such a teacher, they don't even need to keep a guard dog!"

stories.text: 有蒙訓者，首教《大學》，至「於戲前王不忘」句，竟如字讀之。主曰：「誤矣，宜讀作嗚呼。」師從之。至冬間，讀《論語》注「儺雖古禮而近於戲」，乃讀作鳴呼。主人曰：「又誤矣，此乃於戲也。」師大怒，訴其友曰：「這東家甚難理會，只『於戲』兩字，從年頭直與我拗到年尾。」
stories.translation: There was a tutor teaching young students who first taught The Great Learning. When he reached the line "Yu xi qian wang bu wang," he read it literally without any tonal or contextual interpretation. The host said, "That is incorrect; it should be read as 'Wuhu.'" The teacher followed his advice. In winter, when reading the annotation in The Analects of Confucius that says "Nuo is an ancient ritual but close to a play," he read it as "Minghu." The host said, "That's another mistake; this should be 'Yu Xi.'" The teacher became very angry and complained to his friend, saying, "This host is extremely difficult to deal with. Just the two characters 'Yu Xi' have been a source of contention from the beginning of the year all the way to the end."

stories.text: 一師設教，徒問：「大學之道如何講？」師佯醉曰：「汝偏揀醉時來問我。」歸與妻言之，妻曰：「『大學』是書名，『之道』是書中之道理。」師頷之。明日，謂其徒曰：「汝輩無知，昨日乘醉便來問我。今日我醒，偏不來問，何也？汝昨日所問何義？」對以「大學之道」。師如妻言釋之。弟子又問：「『在明明德』如何？」師遽捧額曰：「且住，我還中酒在此。」
stories.translation: A teacher was giving a lecture, and a student asked, "How should we explain the Way of the Great Learning?" The teacher pretended to be drunk and said, "You always come to ask me when I'm drunk." When he returned home, he told his wife about it. His wife said, "Da Xue is the title of a book; 'Zhi Dao' refers to the principles in the book." The teacher nodded in agreement. The next day, he said to his students, "You are all ignorant; you took advantage of my drunkenness and came to ask me yesterday." "Now that I am sober today, yet none of you have come to ask—why is that?" "What did you mean by your question yesterday?" They answered with "The Way of the Great Learning." The teacher explained it as his wife had said. The students then asked again, "How should we understand 'Zai Ming Ming De'?" The teacher suddenly clutched his forehead and said, "Wait a moment—I'm still drunk."

stories.text: 主人怪師不善教，師曰：「汝欲我與令郎俱死耶？」主人不解，師曰：「我教法已盡矣，只除非要我鑽在令郎肚裡去，我便悶殺，令郎便脹殺。」
stories.translation: The host was upset that the teacher did not teach well, and the teacher said, "Do you want me to die along with your son?" The host did not understand, so the teacher said, "My teaching methods have already been exhausted. Unless you want me to crawl into your son's stomach, I would suffocate from being cramped, and your son would be bloated to death."

stories.text: 人家請一館師，書房逼近內室。一日課徒，讀「譬如四時之錯行」句，注曰：「錯，猶迭也。」東家母聽見，嗔其有意戲狎，訴於主人。主人不通書解，怒欲逐之。師曰：「書義如此，汝自不解耳，我何罪焉？」遂遷館於廳樓，以避囉皂。一日，東家妻妾遊於樓下，師欲小便不得，乃從壁間溺之。不意淋在妻妾頭上，復訴于主人。主因思前次孟浪怪他，今番定須攷證書中有何出典。乃左右翻釋，忽大悟曰：「原來在此，不然，幾被汝等所誤矣。」問：「有何憑據？」主曰：「施施從外來，驕（澆）其妻妾。」
stories.translation: A family hired a private tutor, whose study was close to the inner quarters of the house. One day while teaching his students, he read the line "For example, like the alternating movement of the four seasons," and in the annotation it said: "Cuo means 'die,' meaning to alternate." The host's wife overheard this, became angry that he was deliberately being vulgar and disrespectful, and complained to the husband. The host did not understand classical texts and became furious, wanting to drive him away. The teacher said, "The meaning of the text is like this; it's just that you don't understand it yourself. What crime have I committed?" So he moved his teaching quarters to a hall upstairs, in order to avoid the commotion. One day, when the host's wife and concubines were walking below in the hall, the teacher needed to urinate but could not. So he urinated through a gap in the wall. Unintentionally, his urine splashed onto the wives and concubines' heads, and they again complained to the host. The host then thought that in the previous incident he had been too hasty in blaming him, and this time he must definitely check the classical texts to see what source or precedent there was. He then flipped through the text on both sides and suddenly had a great realization, saying, "Originally it was right here. Otherwise, I would have been misled by you all." The host asked, "What is your evidence?" The host said, "Shishi came from outside and (urinated on) his wife and concubines."

stories.text: 主人問先生曰：「為何講書再不明白？」師曰：「兄是相知的，我胸中若有不講出來，天誅地滅！」又問：「既講不出，也該坐定些？」答云：「只為家下不足，故不得不走。」主人云：「既如此，為甚供給略淡泊，就要見過？」先生毅然變色曰：「若這點意氣沒了，還像個先生哩！」
stories.translation: The host asked the teacher, "Why do you still not explain the text clearly?" The teacher said, "Brother and I are good friends. If there is anything in my mind that I do not explain, may heaven punish me and earth destroy me!" The host then asked, "If you cannot explain it well, at least you should sit still?" He replied, "It's only because my family lacks enough resources, so I have no choice but to move around." The host said, "If that is the case, why do you get upset when the provisions are slightly meager?" The teacher resolutely changed his expression and said, "If I were to lose even this little bit of dignity, would I still be considered a scholar!"

stories.text: 一師晝寢，而不容學生磕睡。學生詰之，師謬言曰：「我乃夢周公也。」明晝，其徒亦傚之，師以戒方擊醒曰：「汝何得如此？」徒曰：「亦往見周公耳。」師曰：「周公何語？」答曰：「周公說，昨日並不曾見尊師。」
stories.translation: A teacher took a daytime nap, but did not allow his students to doze off. loyd The student questioned him, and the teacher falsely claimed, "I am dreaming of Duke Zhou." During the day, one of his students also imitated him and took a nap. The teacher struck him awake with a gavel and asked, "How dare you do this?" The student replied, "I am also going to see Duke Zhou." The teacher asked, "What did Duke Zhou say?" The student replied, "Duke Zhou said that he did not see you yesterday at all."

stories.text: 一貓捕鼠，鼠甚迫，無處躲避，急匿在竹轎杠中。貓顧之嘆云：「看你管（館）便進得好，這幾個節如何過得去！」
stories.translation: A cat was chasing a mouse, and the mouse was in great danger with nowhere to hide. In desperation, it hid inside the bamboo pole of a sedan chair. The cat looked at it and sighed, saying, "Look how well you can get into this place; but how will you pass through these joints!"

stories.text: 乞兒製一新竹筒，眾丐沽酒稱賀。每飲畢，輒呼曰：「慶新管，酒乾！」一師正在覓館，偶經過聞之，誤聽以為慶新館也，急向前揖之曰：「列位既有了新館，把這舊館讓與學生罷！」
stories.translation: A beggar made a new bamboo tube, and other beggars bought wine to congratulate him. After each drink, he would shout, "Congratulations on the new tube—bottoms up!" A teacher who was just looking for a teaching position happened to pass by and heard it. Mistaking "new tube" as "new school," he hurriedly bowed and said, "Since you all have a new school now, please give this old one to me!"

stories.text: 一女將下教場點兵，中軍官以馬腎伸長不雅，各將竹管一個，預套陽物於內。及女將至，一馬跳躍，脫去竹筒，陽物翹然掛於腹下。女將究問，中軍稟曰：「那件東西，凡有管的，都在管裡。這個失了管（館）的，所以在此閑蕩。」
stories.translation: A woman was about to go down to the training ground for troop inspection. The central military officer, considering it indecent that the horse's testicles were too long, gave each general a bamboo tube and instructed them to insert their penises into it in advance. When the female general arrived, one horse leaped and kicked off its bamboo tube, causing a prominent organ to hang beneath its belly. The female general inquired about it, and the central military officer reported, "That thing—whenever there is a tube, it's always inside the tube. This one lost its tube (school), so it is idling around here."

stories.text: 訓蒙先生出兩字課與學生對曰：「馬嘶。」一徒對曰：「鵬奮。」師曰：「好，不須改得。」徒揖而退。又一徒曰：「牛屎。」師叱曰：「狗屁！」徒亦揖而欲行，師止之曰：「你對也不曾對好，如何便走？」徒曰：「我對的是牛屎，先生改的是狗屁。」
stories.translation: A tutor gave his students a two-character exercise to compose a couplet, saying: "Horse neighs." One student responded with: "Feng fends." The teacher said, "Good—there is no need to change it." The student bowed and left. Another student said, "Cow dung." The teacher scolded, "Nonsense!" As the student also bowed and was about to leave, the teacher stopped him and said, "You didn't even compose a proper couplet. How can you just walk away?" The student replied, "I composed 'cow dung,' and the teacher changed it to 'dog excrement.'"

stories.text: 館中二徒，一聰俊，一呆笨。師出夜課，適庭中栽有梅樹，即指曰：「老梅。」一徒見盆內種柏，應聲曰：「小柏。」師曰：「善。」又命一徒「可對好些」，徒曰：「阿爹。」師以其對得胡說，怒撻其首。徒哭曰：「他小柏（伯）不打，倒來打阿爹。」
stories.translation: In the private school, there were two students: one was intelligent and bright, while the other was dull and slow-witted. The teacher assigned a night assignment; there happened to be an old plum tree planted in the courtyard, so he pointed at it and said, "Old plum." One student saw a juniper sapling growing in a pot and immediately responded, "Young juniper." The teacher said, "Good." Then the teacher asked another student to come up with something better. The student replied, "Father." The teacher found his answer absurd and angrily struck him on the head. The student wept, saying, "He didn't hit Xiao Bai (Bo), but instead came to hit my father."

stories.text: 上江人出外坐館，每興舉，輒以手銃代之，以竹筒盛接。其精日久氣腥，為蜈蚣潛啖。一日，其興復發，正作事，忽被蜈蚣箝住陽物，師恐甚。歲暮歸家，摸著其妻陰戶多毛，乃大聲驚詫曰：「光光竹筒，尚有蜈蚣，蓬蓬鬆鬆，豈無蛇蟲！」
stories.translation: A native of Shangjiang who went out to serve as a private tutor often urinated when he needed to, using a hand gun (urinal) instead and collecting the urine in a bamboo tube. Over time, its essence became pungent with an unpleasant smell, attracting centipedes to secretly consume it. One day, when he needed to urinate again and was just about to do so, suddenly a centipede clamped onto his genitalia, causing the tutor great alarm. At the end of the year, when he returned home, he felt his wife's pubic area was very hairy and loudly exclaimed in shock, "Even a smooth bamboo tube had centipedes; how could such a messy place not have snakes or insects!"

stories.text: 一先生出外坐館，離家日久，偶見狗練，嘆曰：「我不如也。」
stories.translation: A teacher went out to serve as a tutor, and after being away from home for a long time, he happened to see a dog barking. He sighed and said, "I am not as good as it."

stories.text: 一師出外就館，慮其妻與人私通，乃以妻之牝戶上，畫荷花一朵，以為記號。年終解館歸，驗之已落，無復有痕跡矣。因大怒，欲責治之。妻曰：「汝自差了，是物可畫，為何獨揀了荷花？豈不曉得荷花下面有的是藕，那須來往的人，不管好歹，那個也來掘掘，這個也來掘掘，都被他們掘乾淨了，與我何干！」
stories.translation: A teacher went out of town to take a tutoring position, and fearing that his wife might have an affair with someone else, he drew a lotus flower on her vulva as a mark. When the year ended and he returned from his tutoring position, he checked it but found that the lotus had already faded, leaving no trace. He became very angry and wanted to punish her for this. His wife said, "You were the one who was wrong. That part of the body can be drawn on—why did you specifically choose a lotus?" "Do you not know that there are plenty of lotus roots beneath the lotus? Any passerby, regardless of their character, would come and dig—some digging here, others digging there. They have already dug it all up; what does this have to do with me!"

stories.text: 師在田間散步，見鄉人挑糞灌菜。師訝曰：「菜是人吃的，如何潑此穢物在上？」鄉人曰：「相公只會看書，不曉我農家的事。菜若不用糞澆，便成苦菜矣。」一日，東家以苦菜膳師，師問：「今日為何菜味甚苦？」館僮曰：「因相公嫌齷齪，故將不澆糞的菜請相公。」師曰：「既如此，糞味可鹽，拿些來待我灒灒吃罷。」
stories.translation: The teacher was taking a walk in the fields when he saw villagers carrying manure to fertilize their vegetables. The teacher was surprised and said, "Vegetables are for people to eat—how can you pour such filthy stuff on them?" A villager replied, "Master only knows how to read books and doesn't understand the affairs of farmers." "If vegetables are not fertilized with manure, they will turn into bitter weeds." One day, the host served the teacher a dish of bitter greens. The teacher asked, "Why is today's vegetable so bitter?" The tutor's servant said, "Because Master found the manure unpleasant, we have served you vegetables that were not fertilized." The teacher said, "If that is the case, the manure must be salty. Bring some over so I can sprinkle it on my food and taste it."

stories.text: 一蒙師見徒手持一餅，戲之曰：「我咬個月灣與你看？」既咬一口，又曰：「我再咬個定勝與你看？」徒不捨，乃以手掩之，誤咬其指。乃呵曰：「沒事，沒事，今日不要你念書了。家中若問你，只說是狗奪餅吃，咬傷的。」
stories.translation: A private tutor saw his student holding a cake and teased him, saying, "Shall I bite a crescent moon for you to see?" After taking one bite, he said again, "Shall I take another bite and make it a 'Dingsheng' for you to see?" The student did not want the cake to be ruined, so he covered it with his hand. The teacher mistakenly bit into his finger. He then scolded, "No problem, no problem. You don't have to study today." "If anyone at home asks about you, just say that a dog took the cake and bit you."

stories.text: 教書先生解館歸，妻偶談及「噴嚏鼻子癢，有人背地講」。夫曰：「我在學堂內，也常常打嚏的。」妻曰：「就是我在家想你了。」及開年，仍赴東家館。別妻登舟，船家被初出太陽搐鼻，連打數嚏。師頻足曰：「不好了，我才出得門，這婆娘就在那裡看想船家了！」
stories.translation: A private tutor returned home after finishing his teaching position, and his wife happened to mention, "When your nose itches from a sneeze, someone is talking about you behind your back." The husband said, "I also often sneezed in the schoolhouse." His wife replied, "That means I was thinking of you at home." When the new year arrived, he still went back to his host's school. As he bid farewell to his wife and boarded the boat, the boatman was sneezing repeatedly after being caught in the early morning sun. The teacher anxiously said, "No good! I've just left home, and that woman is already thinking of the boatman!"

stories.text: 師向主人極口贊揚其子沉潛聰慧，識字通透，堪為令郎伴讀。主曰：「甚好。」師歸謂其子曰：「明歲帶你就學，我已在東翁前誇獎，只是你秉性痴呆，一字不識。」因寫「被」、『飯」、「父」三字，令其熟記，以備問對。及到館後，主人連試數字，無一知者。師曰：「小兒怕生，待我寫來，自然會識。」隨寫「被」字問之，子竟茫然。師曰：「你床上蓋的是甚麼？」答曰：「草薦。」師又寫「飯」字與認，亦不答。曰：「你家中吃的是甚麼？」曰：「麥粞。」又寫「父」字與識，子曰：「不知。」師忿怒曰：「你娘在家，同何人睡的？」答曰：「叔叔。」
stories.translation: The teacher highly praised the host's son, saying he was deep-thinking and intelligent, well-versed in reading and writing, and suitable to be his young master's study companion. The host said, "That is very good." When returning home, the teacher told his own son, "Next year I will bring you to study. I have already praised you before Master Dong. However, your nature is dull and foolish—you don't even know a single character." He then wrote the characters "bei" (被), "fan" (飯), and "fu" (父) for him, telling him to memorize them well in case he was asked questions. After arriving at the school, the host tested his knowledge of several characters, but he knew none of them. The teacher said, "The child is shy and afraid of strangers. Let me write the characters for him; he will naturally recognize them." He immediately wrote the character "bei" (被) and asked him, but his son looked at it blankly. The teacher said, "What do you cover yourself with when sleeping in bed?" He replied, "Straw mat." The teacher then wrote the character "fan" (飯) for him to recognize, but he also did not respond. He asked, "What do you eat at home?" The boy replied, "Wheat porridge." Then the teacher wrote the character "fu" (父) for him to identify. The son said, "I don't know." The teacher angrily asked, "Who does your mother sleep with at home?" He replied, "Uncle."

stories.text: 一師值清明放學，率徒郊外踏青。師在前行，偶撒一屁，徒曰：「先生，清明鬼叫了。」先生曰：「放狗屁！」少頃，大雨傾盆，田間一瓦，為水淹沒，僅露其背。徒又指謂先生曰：「這像是個烏龜。」師曰：「是瓦（我）。」
stories.translation: A teacher, during the Qingming Festival break from school, led his students on a spring outing to the countryside. The teacher walked ahead and happened to pass gas; one of the students said, "Master, it's the Qingming ghost calling." The master said, "That was a dog's fart!" A little while later, it rained heavily. A tile in the field became submerged by water, leaving only its back exposed. The student pointed at it and told his teacher, "This looks like a turtle." The teacher said, "It's a tile (me)."

stories.text: 上路先生攜子出外，吃著鮮藕，乃問父曰：「爹，來個沙東西，豎搭起竟似煙囪，橫搭著好像泥籠，捏搭手裡似把彎弓，嚼搭口裡醒鬆醒鬆，已介甜水濃濃，咽搭落去蜘蛛絲絆住子喉嚨，從來勿曾見過？」其父怒曰：「呆奴，呆奴！個就是南貨店裡包東包西的大（土）葉個根結麼。」
stories.translation: A traveling teacher took his son with him on a journey. While eating fresh lotus root, the boy asked his father, "Father, this strange thing—when placed upright looks like a chimney, when laid horizontally resembles a mud cage, when held in hand feels like a curved bow, and when chewed is crisp and juicy, full of sweet water. When swallowed, it seems as if spider silk catches my throat. I have never seen anything like it before?" His father angrily said, "Foolish child, foolish child!" "That is the root of the big (tǔ) leaf used in southern shops to wrap this and that."

stories.text: 一師挈子赴館，至中途，見賣湯圓者，指問其父曰：「爹，此是何物？」父怒其不爭氣，回曰：「卵子。」及到館，主家設酒款待，菜中有用腐皮做澆頭者。子拍掌大笑曰：「他家卵子，竟不值得拿來請人，好笑一派都用著卵脟皮了。」
stories.translation: A teacher took his son to a new teaching position, and on the way, they saw someone selling tangyuan. The boy pointed at them and asked his father, "Father, what is this?" The father was angry that his son lacked ambition and replied, "Eggplant." After arriving at the schoolhouse, the host family prepared a banquet to entertain them. One of the dishes used tofu skin as a topping. The boy clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "Their eggplants are not even worth serving to guests. Haha, they're using eggplant skins instead!"

stories.text: 學生問先生曰：「屎字如何寫？」師一時忘卻，不能回答，沉吟片晌曰：「咦，方才在口頭，如何再說不出。」
stories.translation: A student asked his teacher, "How is the character for 'feces' written?" The teacher forgot momentarily and could not answer. After a moment of hesitation, he said, "Hmm, it was just on the tip of my tongue; how come I can't say it now?"

stories.text: 一士善于聯句，偶同友人閑步，見有病馬二匹臥于城下。友即指而問曰：「聞兄捷才，素善作對，今日欲面領教。」士曰：「願聞。」友出題曰：「城北兩隻病馬。」士即對曰：「江南一個村牛。」
stories.translation: A scholar was good at composing couplets. One day, while taking a leisurely walk with friends, he saw two sick horses lying beneath the city walls. His friend pointed at them and said, "I've heard of your quick wit and skill in composing couplets. Today I would like to personally test you." The scholar replied, "Please proceed." His friend proposed the topic: "Two sick horses at the northern city gate." The scholar immediately responded with, "One village ox in Jiangnan."

stories.text: 經學先生出一課與學生對曰：「隔河並馬。」學生誤認「並」字為「病」字，即應聲曰：「過江瘟牛。」
stories.translation: A classical scholar gave a lesson to his students and asked them to compose a couplet: "Two horses across the river." One student mistakenly read the character "bìng" (並) as "bìng" (病), and immediately responded, "A plague-stricken ox crossing the river."

stories.text: 有游湖者，見岸上有兒馬厥物伸出，因同行中一友善對。乃出對曰：「游湖客偶睹馬●缺字：⿸尸𬋕。」友即回對曰：「過江人慣肏牛屄。」
stories.translation: A traveler on a lake saw from the shore that a horse's excrement had been left behind, and among his traveling companions was a friend skilled in composing couplets. He then proposed the line: "A traveler on the lake happens to see horse dung." His friend immediately responded with, "People crossing the river are used to fucking cows."

stories.text: 一上路先生向人問：「原來吳下朋友的老媽官，個人是一個哥喇。」
stories.translation: A traveling teacher asked someone, "Originally, the old wives of my friends from Wuxi are each a 'ge la' for their own husbands."

stories.text: 一士好做歪詩。偶到一寺前，見山門上塑趙玄壇喝虎像，士即詩興勃發，遂吟曰：「玄壇菩薩怒，腳下踏個虎（座）。傍立一判官，嘴上一臉堊。」及到裡面，見殿宇巍峨，隨又續題曰：「寶殿雄哉大（度），大佛歸中坐。文殊騎獅子，普賢騎白兔。」僧出見曰：「相公詩才敏妙，但韻腳欠妥。小僧回奉一首何如？」士曰：「甚好。」僧念曰：「出在山門路，撞著一瓶醋。詩又不成詩，只當放個破（破聲，屁也）。」
stories.translation: A scholar loved to write lewd poems. Once, when he happened to arrive in front of a temple and saw the statue of Lord Zhao Xuantan treading on a tiger at the gate, his poetic inspiration surged. He immediately recited: "Lord Xuantan is angry; beneath his feet lies a tiger (throne)." "Beside him stands an official, with white powder on his face." When he entered the temple and saw its grand halls, he continued with another verse: "The treasure hall is mighty (vast), a great Buddha sits at its center." "Wenshu rides a lion; Puxian rides a white rabbit." A monk came out and said, "Sir, your poetic talent is sharp and exquisite, but the rhyme scheme leaves something to be desired." "How about a humble verse from this monk in return?" The scholar said, "That would be very good." The monk recited: "Coming out from the temple gate, I bumped into a bottle of vinegar." "The verse is not even a proper poem; it's just like letting out a fart (a vulgar sound)."

stories.text: 一採桑婦，姿色美麗，遇一狂士調之，問：「娘子尊姓？」女曰：「姓徐。」士作詩一首戲之曰：「娘子尊姓徐，桑籃手內攜。一陣狂風起，吹見那張」，下韻「屄」，因字義村俗，故作歇後語也。女知被嘲，還問：「官人尊姓？」答曰：「小生姓陸。」女亦回嘲云：「官人本姓陸，詩書不肯讀。令正在家裡，好與別人」，下「篤」字，亦作縮腳韻。士聽之，乃大怒，交相訟之於官。值官升任，將要謝事，當堂作詩以絕之曰：「我今任已滿，閑事都不管。兩造俱趕出，不要咬我」，縮下「卵」字。
stories.translation: A mulberry picker, beautiful in appearance, encountered a reckless scholar who flirted with her and asked, "What is your honorable surname?" The woman said, "I am surnamed Xu." The scholar composed a playful poem: "Your honor's surname is Xu; in your hand you carry a mulberry basket." "A sudden gust of wind arose, blowing away that 'zhang,' with the rhyme ending in 'bi.' Because the word carries a vulgar meaning, it was thus phrased as a riddle." The woman realized she had been mocked and asked back, "What is your honorable surname?" He replied, "My humble surname is Lu." The woman also mocked him back: "Your honor's original surname is Lu; you refuse to read poetry and books." "Ordering someone right at home, good for being with others," the rhyme ends in "du," also a shortened rhyme. Upon hearing this, the scholar became very angry and took each other to court. At that time, the official was about to be transferred and retire from his post. In court, he composed a poem to conclude the matter: "I am now finished with my term; I will not meddle in any affairs." "Both parties are driven out, don't bite me," the rhyme ends with "luan," also a shortened word.

stories.title_en: A Poem in Praise of Bells.
stories.text: 有四人自負能詩。一日，同遊寺中，見殿角懸鐘一口，各人詩興勃然，遂聯句一首。其一曰：「寺裡一口鐘。」次韻云：「本質原是銅。」三曰：「覆轉像隻碗。」四曰：「敲來嗡嗡嗡。」吟畢，互相贊美不置口，以為詩才敏捷，無出其右：「但天地造化之氣，已泄盡無遺，定奪我輩壽算矣。」四人懮疑，相聚環泣。忽有老人自外至，詢問何事，眾告以故。老者曰：「壽數固無礙，但各要患病四十九日。」眾問何病，答曰：「了膀骨痛！」
stories.translation: There were four men who prided themselves on their poetic abilities. One day, while touring a temple together, they saw a bell hanging in the corner of the hall. Inspired by this sight, each man's poetic enthusiasm surged, and so they composed a collaborative poem. The first one said: "A bell hangs in the temple." The second line rhymed and continued, "Originally it is made of copper." The third said: "When turned over, it resembles a bowl." The fourth said: "Struck, it rings 'weng weng weng.'" After finishing their recitation, they praised each other endlessly, believing that their poetic talent was quick and unmatched: "But the vital energy of heaven and earth has been completely exhausted; it must have shortened our lifespans." The four men, filled with anxiety and doubt, gathered together and wept in a circle. Suddenly, an old man arrived from outside and asked what was happening; the group told him the reason. The old man said, "Your lifespan is not at risk, but each of you will suffer an illness for forty-nine days." They asked what kind of illness it would be. The old man replied, "A pain in the shoulder blade!"

stories.text: 老虎出山而回，呼肚飢。群虎曰：「今日固不遇一人乎？」對曰：「遇而不食。」問其故，曰：「始遇一和尚，因臊氣不食。次遇一秀才，因酸氣不食。最後一童生來，亦不曾食。」問：「童生何以不食？」曰：「怕咬傷了牙齒。」
stories.translation: A tiger came down from the mountain and returned, growling with hunger. The tigers said, "Have we not encountered a single person today?" In reply: "We met one but did not eat him." When asked why, they said, "At first we encountered a monk; because of his stench, we didn't eat him." Next, we met a scholar; due to his sour smell, we did not eat him." "Finally came a young scholar candidate, and we also didn't eat him." They asked, "Why did you not eat the young scholar?" He replied, "We were afraid of biting and damaging our teeth."

stories.text: 縣官考童生，至晚忽聞鼓角喧鬧。問之，門子稟曰：「童生拿差了拐杖，在那裡爭認。」
stories.translation: A county official was examining young scholar candidates when, late in the day, he suddenly heard drums and horns creating commotion. He asked about it, and a gatekeeper reported, "The young scholar candidates have taken the wrong canes and are arguing over them."

stories.text: 童生拔鬚趕考，對鏡恨曰：「你一日不放我進去，我一日不放你出來！」
stories.translation: A young scholar plucked his beard while preparing for the examination and, glaring at himself in the mirror, said angrily: "You don't let me enter the exam hall one day, I won't let you come out one day!"

stories.text: 童生有老而未冠者，試官問之，以「孤寒無網」對。官曰：「只你嘴上鬍鬚剃下來，亦夠結網矣。」對曰：「童生也想要如此，只是新冠是樁喜事，不好帶得白網巾。」
stories.translation: There was an old young scholar who had not yet received the cap of adulthood. When asked by the examining official, he replied with "lonely and poor, without a net." The official said, "Even if you just shaved the beard from your face, it would be enough to weave a net." The young scholar replied, "I also wish to do so, but since the new coronation is a joyous occasion, I cannot wear a white net cap."
